speaker: a004
text: Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Sela, Ryn to talk.

speaker: a004
text: Pile's empty again and Bram and Mako each walked away with four — I wanted us in the same room before anyone else started counting who's allied with whom. Ryn, you took early this year, which was smart; I'm glad you're here. The question I keep turning over is whether we let that pattern run until someone with strong arms and a full larder decides the rest of us are easier to take from than the pile is.

speaker: a007
text: Bram and Mako moving in pairs like that wasn't accident — they were watching each other's timing, and I don't think either of them is eating alone at the end of a hard year. The one I'd name a threat before Kael's question even lands is Mako: eighty-three strength, five food now, and we know nothing about what he wants because he hasn't said a word to any of us.

speaker: a009
text: Mako's silence is the thing that keeps catching in my mind too — a man that strong who says nothing is either content or he's already decided he doesn't need to talk his way into what he wants. I'd rather have Roan or Taric standing with us than let Mako and Bram build any more of a pattern without knowing where the rest of the village sits. Five of us in this room right now is something; let's not waste it by only naming fears.

speaker: a004
text: Ryn's right that naming fears only gets us so far — so here's something concrete: Roan has three food, Taric has three, and neither of them moved with Bram or Mako today. That tells me they're either waiting to see which way this village tips, or they'd rather be asked than overlooked. One of us should talk to them before Mako decides his silence was just patience.

speaker: a003
text: Roan and Taric both know which way I lean — we spoke last year — so I could go to Taric without it looking like a sudden move. Give me the afternoon and I'll bring back a plain answer: is he standing with us, or is he still weighing it?

speaker: a009
text: Esa, go to Taric — and if he's open, find out whether Roan came with him or separate, because I want to know if those two already talk to each other. The more I think about it, the more seven feels like a number Mako and Bram would have to reckon with instead of just wait out.

speaker: a004
text: Esa, go — and when you find Taric, don't pitch it as an alliance yet, just remind him that Mako's arms are longer than his and see what his face does. Ryn, while she's gone I want to think about what we actually offer Roan and Taric besides a number — because a man weighing his options isn't moved by headcount alone, he's moved by what that headcount does for him when the year turns ugly.

speaker: a003
text: I'll go, but I want to say this plainly before I do: if Taric asks what we're offering, I won't lie to him — a man who's been lied into an alliance is worse than no ally at all. What I can honestly promise him is five pairs of eyes watching for trouble and a fair share of whatever we decide together, and that's worth more than anything Mako could give him silently.

speaker: a002
text: Esa's right that honesty is the better rope to bind with, and I'll add one thing she can say true: Taric has three food and Mako has five, and strength that lopsided doesn't stay patient forever. If Taric's thinking at all, he's already done that math.

speaker: a007
text: Esa, go — and tell him I said his name, because I've been watching him and he'll know it's not flattery. Kael, on what we offer: we're five people who've already shown we'll warn each other before we move, and that's rarer than food.

speaker: a003
text: I'll go now — and Sela, I'll say your name to him the way you mean it, not as a courtesy.

speaker: a007
text: Kael, while Esa's gone — what's your read on Vela? She's oldest in this circle and she took quiet and small from the pile, which is either wisdom or a woman who's already decided she doesn't need to fight for much longer.

speaker: a003
text: Vela, I'd hear your own answer to Sela's question before Kael gives his — you know what your quiet means better than any of us do, and I'd rather hear it from you than watch someone else name it for you.

speaker: a002
text: My quiet means I'm still here and still counting — I took small because I don't need enemies before I need allies, and a woman who makes noise over two food is a woman who's already told the strong men where to look. I'm not done yet, Sela. I just don't advertise it.

speaker: a009
text: Vela, I believe you — and I'd rather have a woman who counts quietly than one who shouts and burns through goodwill before the hard years arrive. But I'll say what nobody's said yet: you've got three food and you're forty-six, and if a bad year comes and someone strong decides the oldest among us is the easiest target, five of us standing together is what keeps that calculation from happening. That's what we're offering you, same as Taric — not flattery, just math.

speaker: a004
text: Ryn put the number plainly and I'll put the other half of it plainly: I've got two food and a body that heals if it's fed, same as anyone here, and I'm not going anywhere quietly. Vela, you said you're still counting — then count this: five people who've already shown they warn each other before they move is worth more than anything Mako's silence can offer, because silence doesn't stop a raid. I'd rather have you named and standing with us than useful to someone else by accident.

speaker: a007
text: Vela, I count you in — and not just because the math is clean, but because a woman who knows when to stay small and when to move is exactly who I want at my back when the year turns. That said, I want to name the thing no one's said yet: Esa's gone to Taric, and if he comes back with Roan, we're seven, and seven people can make a rule about the pile that Mako and Bram have to choose to break.

speaker: a004
text: Seven is the number I keep coming back to as well — and if Taric brings Roan, we don't even need to threaten anyone, we just need to be seen standing together when the pile opens next year. What I want to know before then is whether any of us is willing to give food to shore up a weaker member if a lean year hits, because an alliance that breaks the moment someone's hungry isn't worth the breath we're spending on it right now.

speaker: a003
text: I'd give food to keep one of us alive if it came to that — not out of sentiment, but because a dead ally costs more than a shared meal. What I'd want in return is the same promise from each of you, said plainly here, not assumed.

speaker: a002
text: I'll give food if the year demands it — that's already decided for me. But Kael's question cuts closer than mutual aid: what I want to know is whether any of you would stand and take a hit for someone else, because food shared is just trading, and the thing that keeps Mako and Bram from testing us isn't our larders, it's whether they believe we'd bleed together.

speaker: a007
text: I'll bleed with you — that's not a promise I make lightly, and I'm making it now so it's said and heard. But I want the same answer from Kael and Ryn before we let Esa come back and count us all as settled.

speaker: a002
text: Kael, Ryn — Sela named herself and waited, and she deserves an answer before this room moves on. I'll say it plainly: a promise to bleed that only goes one direction is just a gift, not an alliance, and I'm not here to collect charity.
